name: RTS Action Replay
description: Capture OBS replay-buffer clips and play them through a Streamer.bot controlled browser overlay.\nUses its own [[blue:fully featured catalog]], with search capabilities. Over [[blue:39 commands]] for complete control through chat on all supported platforms.\nThe Settings interface allows customisation of [[blue:colours]], [[blue:layout]] and [[blue:behaviour]].

website.footerLabel: Part of The Road to Somewhere.

experience.title: Turn OBS replay clips into an interactive on-stream replay player.
experience.text: RTS Action Replay connects OBS Replay Buffer captures, Streamer.bot and a remote browser overlay so saved clips can be loaded and controlled without a separate web server.

features.title: Supports Twitch, YouTube and Kick
features.text: Full support for Twitch, YouTube, and Kick (via kickbot or kick), Capture clips directly from the platform's chat, and catalog them. Full cross-platform capabilities, with automatic platform branding depending on which platform initiated the command.

features.title: Complete Branding control
features.text: Customise the Brand Colours, Logo, and fonts to fit your stream. 4 Design presets to choose from. Choose different presets for different platforms.

features.title: Full catalog with search, rating and leaderboards
features.text: Complete catalog of all your clips, with full searching by date, creator, and rating. Leaderboards keep track of top clippers and clip requestors. Full playlist functionality to queue multiple requested clips.

features.title: Remote or local overlay
features.text: A complete, functioning overlay to perform all the actions you need, with a dev mode for complete testing of the extension

features.title: Complete layout control with full animation
features.text: Complete control with our positioning system lets you position the Player, Search Panels, and Overlay Messages wherever you want, and create entry/exit animations for them with ease.

features.title: Include complete set of Chat commands
features.text: Chat commands for everything: clipping, Queuing, Catalog Searching, Playlist control, and video control.

requirements: Streamer.bot with its WebSocket and HTTP servers enabled.
RtsUI.dll for the extension settings interface.

setup.title: Get Action Replay running.
setup.intro: Import the Streamer.bot actions, enable them, configure OBS Replay Buffer and the local HTTP file mapping, add the overlay to OBS, then test Action Replay.

steps.title: Import the extension into Streamer.bot
steps.description: Open Streamer.bot and use Import to paste the supplied import string, or download the latest import file and import it into Streamer.bot.

substeps.title: Copy the import string
substeps.text: Look above for Action Import, click the Copy Import button, then paste the import code into Streamer.bot's Import dialog.

images.alt: The RTS extension import code with an arrow pointing to the import code button

substeps.title: Open Import
substeps.text: Select Import from the Streamer.bot toolbar.

images.alt: Streamer.bot import screen showing the RTS extension import code

substeps.title: Paste the import code
substeps.text: Paste the supplied import string into the Import String box, then select Import.

substeps.title: Confirm the import
substeps.text: Review the actions being imported, then select Import to continue.

steps.title: Enable the imported actions
steps.description: Enable the imported RTS Action Replay actions and commands so the extension can respond to events and chat commands.

substeps.title: Enable the extension actions
substeps.text: Enable the imported RTS Action Replay actions in Streamer.bot.

images.alt: Streamer.bot imported RTS actions being enabled

substeps.title: Check and Enable the commands
substeps.text: Confirm the imported RTS Action Replay commands are present and enabled where required.

images.alt: Streamer.bot commands showing the imported RTS Action Replay commands

steps.title: Enable OBS Replay Buffer
steps.description: If you want to enable capturing of local files created by the OBS Replay Buffer, choose the folder where the replay files are saved.

substeps.title: Enable Replay Buffer
substeps.text: In OBS, open Settings > Output and enable Replay Buffer.

substeps.title: Choose the replay folder
substeps.text: Configure OBS to save replay files to a folder that Streamer.bot can access. You will use this same folder when configuring the HTTP Server mapping and RTS Action Replay settings.

steps.title: Configure the Streamer.bot HTTP Server
steps.description: The hosted RTS overlay cannot read files directly from your computer. Streamer.bot's HTTP Server provides the local URL that the overlay uses to load replay video files.

substeps.title: Enable the HTTP Server
substeps.text: In Streamer.bot, open the Servers or Web Server settings and enable the HTTP Server. Keep note of the HTTP port.

images.alt: Setting up the HTTP Server in Streamer.bot

substeps.title: Add a file mapping
substeps.text: Create a file or directory mapping for the OBS Replay Buffer folder. Use a simple URL path such as [[code:replays]] and point it to the same local folder where OBS saves replay files. If you want to save Twitch and Kick clips locally. add mapping for those too.

substeps.title: Check the mapping
substeps.text: The mapping should point to the replay folder that OBS saves its buffer to.

images.alt: Mappings section of the HTTP server settings

substeps.title: Keep the HTTP server available
substeps.text: Leave the Streamer.bot HTTP Server running while using Action Replay. The overlay uses this service to request the local replay video. It's recommended to turn on the toggle at the top of the HTTP settings to have the HTTP server auto-start on launch.

steps.title: Enable the Streamer.bot WebSocket
steps.description: The hosted overlay uses the Streamer.bot WebSocket to receive Action Replay events and commands.

substeps.title: Enable the WebSocket Server
substeps.text: In Streamer.bot, open the WebSocket Server settings and enable the server. Keep the configured port available to the overlay.

substeps.title: Keep WebSocket access available
substeps.text: The Streamer.bot WebSocket Server must remain running while the Action Replay overlay is in use. It's recommended to turn on the toggle at the top of the WebSocket settings to have the WebSocket server auto-start on launch.

steps.title: Add the Action Replay overlay to OBS
steps.description: Add the Action Replay hosted overlay as an OBS Browser Source, or use the supplied local overlay files.

substeps.title: Copy the Overlay URL
substeps.text: Look above in the Quick Access section and click the Copy Overlay URL button. This copies the overlay URL to your clipboard for use in OBS.

images.alt: RTS Copy Overlay URL button screenshot

substeps.title: Create a browser source
substeps.text: Add a Browser Source to an existing or newly created scene in OBS.

images.alt: OBS add a new browser source dialog

substeps.title: Configure the browser source
substeps.text: Paste the Overlay URL you just copied into the URL field, then set the width and height to 1920x1080 or another 16:9 size. The Action Replay overlay uses a 1920x1080 coordinate system. Enable Refresh browser when scene becomes active if required by your scene setup.

steps.title: Configure RTS Action Replay Settings
steps.description: Open the RTS Action Replay settings and configure the extension.

substeps.title: Open the settings dialog
substeps.text: In the Streamer.bot Actions panel, look for RTS Action Replay settings action to open the extension settings. The settings are fully documented below in [yellow: Action Replay Documentation]

images.alt: Streamer.bot commands showing the imported RTS Action Replay commands

substeps.title: Automatic installation of RtsUI.dll
substeps.text: If you do not have the DLL installed, the extension can download and place it in your Streamer.bot installation directory. If you do not see the install prompt, it may be hiding behind another window. Check your taskbar for a Streamer.bot dialog and bring it to the front.

substeps.title: Automatic updating of RtsUI.dll
substeps.text: If the extension requires an updated version, it can ask whether you want to download and install the latest version. If you do not see the update prompt, it may be hiding behind another window. Check your taskbar for a Streamer.bot dialog and bring it to the front.

steps.title: Test Action Replay Setup and Configuration
steps.description: Test and set up the Extension using the overlay's built-in development mode.

substeps.title: Put the overlay into dev mode
substeps.text: Copy the [[overlay:Overlay URL]], open it in a browser, and add [[muted: ?dev=true]] at the end.\n\nThis will put the overlay into dev mode, where you can test the extension's features.

substeps.title: Send the current config to the overlay
substeps.text: In the Test tab of the extension's settings, you can click the Send Configuration to Overlay button. Once this is done, all the presets will be sent to the overlay and can be previewed.

images.alt: Send the configuration to the dev overlay

substeps.title: Use the test harness to preview your current settings.
substeps.text: The Testing tab of the settings allows you to send various actions to the overlay so you can preview your changes easily.\p\pAfter changing an option in the test settings, click save before initiating a test.

documentation.title: Action Replay Documentation
documentation.intro: Reference documentation for configuring and using RTS Action Replay.

sections.title: Settings
sections.intro: Configure Action Replay in the same order as the Streamer.bot settings window.

sections.title: Local Capture
sections.intro: Configure how RTS discovers, registers, and serves local OBS Replay Buffer captures.

sections.title: Local Capture / OBS
controls: Folder containing local OBS Replay Buffer files. Twitch and Kick downloads use separate folders.
File extensions accepted when scanning or registering files from the Replay Folder. Separate multiple extensions with commas, for example [[code:.mp4, .mkv]].
URL path used in the local replay URL. It must match the Streamer.bot HTTP server mapping serving the Replay Folder.
Port used in the local replay URL. It must match Streamer.bot's HTTP server port.

sections.title: Replay Defaults
controls: Generates the title of a newly added OBS replay. Available variables are [[code:%replayName%]], [[code:%replayDate%]] and [[code:%replayTime%]]. A manually supplied title bypasses the template.

sections.title: Local Capture Handling
controls: Adds each newly saved OBS replay to the Catalog. It also becomes available to Recent Clips through the Catalog's recent history.
Adds a newly saved OBS replay to the playback queue for playback.
notes: When automatic registration is disabled, existing replay files can still be registered with Add Replay or Scan Replays.

sections.title: Twitch
sections.intro: Configure how Twitch clips are acquired and made available to the player.

sections.title: Twitch Clips
controls: Use the Twitch URL, download locally, or support both methods. In Both mode, a local copy is preferred and Twitch is the fallback.
Folder used for downloaded Twitch clips. It must be separate from the OBS Replay Folder.
URL path used by Streamer.bot to serve downloaded Twitch clips. The shared HTTP Port is configured under Local Capture / OBS.
Default duration used by Twitch clip commands when no duration is supplied.
notes: The allowed Twitch clip duration is 5-60 seconds. A duration supplied with the command overrides the setting within that range.

sections.title: Twitch Clip Playback
bullets: [[code:Download Locally]] - download and play a local copy through Streamer.bot's HTTP server.
[[code:Both]] - use the local copy when available and fall back to Twitch playback when it is unavailable.

sections.title: YouTube
sections.intro: Configure timestamp-based clips from the current monitored YouTube broadcast.

sections.title: YouTube Clips
controls: Default duration used by YouTube clip commands when no duration is supplied.
notes: The allowed duration is 5-60 seconds. Action Replay uses the current broadcast and its monitored start time to calculate the clip timestamp.

sections.title: Kick
sections.intro: Configure how Kick clips are acquired and made available to the player.

sections.title: Kick Clips
controls: Use the Kick URL, download locally, or support both methods. In Both mode, a local copy is preferred and direct Kick playback is the fallback.
Folder used for downloaded Kick clips. It must be separate from the OBS Replay Folder.
URL path used by Streamer.bot to serve downloaded Kick clips. The shared HTTP Port is configured under Local Capture / OBS.

sections.title: Kick Clip Playback
bullets: [[code:Download Locally]] - download and play a local copy through Streamer.bot's HTTP server.
[[code:Both]] - use the local copy when available and fall back to direct Kick playback when necessary.

sections.title: Playback
sections.intro: Control how replays start and how playback controls and player styling are presented.

sections.title: Playback
controls: Displays the Play/Pause control and interactive playback progress bar.
Displays the interactive playback progress bar.
Playback speed used when a replay is loaded. Range 0.25-2.0.
Controls when the playback speed indicator is displayed.
Only when greater or less than 1

sections.title: Player Appearance
controls: Uses a Custom, Branding Primary or Branding Secondary colour for the player frame.
Custom frame colour when Frame Colour Source is Custom.
Uses a Custom, Branding Primary or Branding Secondary colour for the Play/Pause control and progress bar.
Custom control colour when Control Colour Source is Custom.
Adds a branded glow around the player border.
notes: Change Player Branding to Clip Source is configured later under Player Behaviour. When enabled, it can override the player frame and control branding with the active source branding.

sections.title: Catalog
sections.intro: The Catalog is the persistent replay library. Recent Clips and Last Played are different views/history derived from replay data, while the Playlist is the live playback queue.

sections.title: Recent Clips
controls: Maximum number of entries shown in Recent Clips and retained in Last Played history. Older Catalog entries remain available.
Maximum number of results shown per Catalog/search page. The [[code:--amount]] option can request a different page size up to this limit.

sections.title: Live Playlist
sections.intro: The Playlist is the live, source-agnostic playback queue. It can contain OBS captures, Twitch clips, YouTube clips and Kick clips.
controls: Keeps the current Playlist queue when Streamer.bot restarts. Active playback and pause state are not persisted.

sections.title: Branding Presets
sections.intro: Define reusable colours, typography and branding identity used by Player, Panel, Clapperboard and Message presentation.
controls: Display name used in settings and selection lists.
Optional Twitch, Kick or YouTube association.
Google Font used by player titles, panel titles and branding.
Font size used by player and panel titles.
HTTPS URL of the branding logo.
Text used when the branding logo cannot be loaded.
Label displayed with the logo or fallback text.
notes: A preset can optionally be associated with Twitch, Kick or YouTube. Source-platform branding is enabled independently by Player, Panel, Message and Clapperboard Behaviour settings.
If a matching platform preset is unavailable, the relevant Behaviour setting's configured Branding Preset is used as the fallback.

sections.title: Design Presets
sections.intro: Define the visual treatment used by Player, Panel and Message presentation.

sections.title: Available designs
notes: Broadcast and Cut expose additional configuration in the settings window. Cinematic and Minimal currently have no design-specific controls.

sections.title: Broadcast
sections.intro: Provides the animated chevron treatment.
notes: Controls include the background source/colour and chevron height, width, spacing, speed and randomisation.

sections.title: Cut
sections.intro: Provides the block/bar treatment.
notes: Controls include the background source/colour, block width, block-width randomisation and bar height.
Design Presets are assigned through the relevant Behaviour section.

sections.title: Title Presets
sections.intro: Define how replay titles are positioned, decorated and animated in the Player.
controls: Places the decoration before or after the title.
Places the title at the top or bottom of the player.
Text displayed as the title prefix/suffix.
Delay before the title is shown, in milliseconds.
Time the title remains displayed, in milliseconds.
Duration of the title animation, in milliseconds.
notes: The built-in Default Title Preset is permanent. Additional Title Presets can be created and removed.

sections.title: Positions
sections.intro: Define reusable Player, Panel, Message and Clapperboard positions in the shared 1920x1080 overlay coordinate space.

sections.title: Player Positions
sections.intro: Saved positions used by Player Animation and playback.
notes: The player editor also supports the player field-of-view transform used by the overlay.

sections.title: Panel Positions
sections.intro: Saved positions used by Panel Animation and panel playback.
controls: Information panel width in 1920x1080 output pixels.
Information panel height in 1920x1080 output pixels.
Information panel corner radius in pixels.

sections.title: Message Positions
sections.intro: Saved positions used by Message Animation and playback.
controls: Fixed message width in 1920x1080 output pixels.
Fixed message height in 1920x1080 output pixels.
Message panel corner radius in pixels.
notes: Message text scales to fit the configured message dimensions.

sections.title: Clapperboard Positions
sections.intro: Saved positions used by Clapperboard Animation and playback.

notes: All four position editors support saved transforms including scale, X/Y/Z position and X/Y/Z rotation. Animation Profiles reference these saved positions, so changing a saved position affects every profile that uses it.

sections.title: Player Animation Profiles
sections.intro: Define reusable Player animation profiles with separate Start and End sequences.
notes: Each sequence contains Position, Duration, Easing and Delay. Easing values are linear, ease, ease-in, ease-out and ease-in-out. Duration and delay support 0-60,000 milliseconds.
The built-in Default profile is permanent and editable. Additional profiles can be created and removed.
Profiles are assigned through Player Behaviour.

sections.title: Panel Animation Profiles
sections.intro: Define reusable Panel animation profiles with separate Start and End sequences. Steps use saved Panel Positions with configurable duration, easing and delay.
notes: The built-in Default profile is permanent and editable. Additional profiles can be created and removed.
Profiles are assigned through Panel Behaviour.

sections.title: Message Animation Profiles
sections.intro: Define reusable Message animation profiles with separate Start and End sequences. Steps use saved Message Positions with configurable duration, easing and delay.
notes: The built-in Default profile is permanent and editable. Additional profiles can be created and removed.
The selected profile is used by Message Behaviour.

sections.title: Clapperboard Animation Profiles
sections.intro: Define reusable Clapperboard animation profiles with separate Start and End sequences. Steps use saved Clapperboard Positions with configurable duration, easing and delay.
notes: The built-in Default profile is permanent and editable. Additional profiles can be created and removed.
The selected profile is used by Clapperboard Behaviour.

sections.title: Player Behaviour
sections.intro: Configure the Player presentation for each replay entry point.
controls: Selects the Animation Profile, Design Preset, Title Preset and Branding Preset used for OBS-created replays.
Selects the presentation presets used for Twitch-created clips.
Selects the presentation presets used for YouTube-created clips.
Selects the presentation presets used for Kick-created clips.
Selects the presentation presets used when a replay is played.
For newly created clips, selects the Branding Preset associated with the clip's source platform when a matching preset exists.
Change Player Branding to Clip Source
When enabled, each replay uses the Branding Preset assigned to the replay creator's platform. The player frame, design colours, buttons and progress bar follow that branding.

sections.title: Panel Behaviour
sections.intro: Configure the presentation for Recent / Search, Playlist and Leaderboards.
notes: Each entry point selects an Animation Profile, Design Preset, Title Preset and Branding Preset.
Use Source Platform Branding can override the configured branding when a matching platform preset exists. The platform is the platform that initiated the panel command.

sections.title: Message Behaviour
sections.intro: Configure how transient messages are presented in the overlay.
controls: Branding used by transient messages, with source-platform fallback when enabled.
Time the message remains visible before its end animation begins, in milliseconds.
Uses the platform that initiated the message to select matching branding when available.
notes: Messages use fixed dimensions configured under Message Positions and scale text to fit those dimensions. If no matching platform Branding Preset exists, the configured Message Behaviour Branding Preset is used.

sections.title: Clapperboard Behaviour
sections.intro: Configure the Clapperboard used when a new replay is created.
controls: Uses the Clapperboard for Replay Created instead of the Message system when Replay Created Overlay is enabled.
Uses the Branding Preset associated with the platform that created the clip when available.
Animation profile used by the Clapperboard.
Fallback branding used when source-platform branding is disabled or unavailable.
Time the Clapperboard remains visible before its end animation begins, in milliseconds.
notes: The Clapperboard is a separate presentation from normal Message Outputs.

sections.title: Messages
sections.intro: Configure where list results are presented and how lifecycle messages are generated.

sections.title: Search Presentation
controls: Shows Catalog/search results in the Search Panel.
Sends one formatted chat message for the search header and each result.
notes: Both can be enabled at the same time.

sections.title: Playlist and Recent Clips Presentation
controls: Sends one formatted chat message for each Recent Clips entry.
Sends one formatted chat message for each Playlist entry.
Format used for each list entry.
Maximum length of each individual list entry/message. Longer entries are truncated rather than split.
notes: List entry variables are [[code:%listNumber%]], [[code:%title%]], [[code:%creator%]], [[code:%rating%]], [[code:%platform%]] and [[code:%plays%]].

sections.title: Replay Messages
sections.intro: Replay lifecycle notifications are configured under Replays, Playlist and Updates.
notes: Each event has message text and a Chat toggle. Events that support overlay output also have an Overlay toggle.
Replay Created uses the separate Clapperboard presentation when Use Clapperboard is enabled. The other overlay-capable lifecycle events use the Message presentation.
Overlay messages are queued centrally. Chat messages are sent immediately. An overlay message is considered finished only when its exit animation completes.
Replay Queued is generated only when the Playlist already contained an item before the new replay was added.

sections.title: Import Settings
sections.intro: Import selected RTS Action Replay settings from a JSON file.
notes: The Import dialog controls which configuration areas, profiles and Catalog data are included and handles duplicate profiles.

sections.title: Export Settings
sections.intro: Export the complete RTS Action Replay configuration to a JSON file.
notes: Export includes the configuration snapshot and supported global settings.

sections.title: Factory Reset
sections.intro: Restore RTS Action Replay configuration to its built-in defaults.
notes: Factory Reset preserves the Catalog and play history. Configuration globals are reset and required defaults are recreated.

sections.title: Configuration Sync
sections.intro: Send Configuration to Overlay sends the complete current Action Replay configuration to the overlay for configuration-sync testing.

sections.title: Player
controls: Selects the simulated requester platform and chat routing.
Independently selects the source platform of the test replay.
Plays the first Catalog replay using the current Player presentation settings without adding it to the Playlist or play history.
Shows a representative panel using the first Catalog replay and current Panel presentation settings.
Shows the Clapperboard for the first Catalog replay using the current Clapperboard presentation settings.

sections.title: Messages
controls: Selects the lifecycle message simulated by Test Message.
Selects either the current Message settings or the selected Design and Branding overrides.
When Test Source is Override, selects the presentation design used for the test.
When Test Source is Override, selects the presentation branding used for the test.
Shows the selected message using the first Catalog replay. Chat output follows the selected Test Origin.

sections.title: Commands
sections.intro: Command reference for the current Streamer.bot action mappings.

sections.title: Catalog
commands: Add one existing OBS replay file from the configured Replay Folder to the Catalog. If no title is supplied, the Replay Title Template is used. Existing Catalog entries are not added again.
Search for replays from a date period. Supported forms include today, this week, last week, this year, last year, year, month and month year.
Delete Catalog entries from the current result set. Multiple current-page results can be supplied as comma-separated numbers. The physical media file is not deleted.
Return to the first page of the current Catalog/search results.
Jump to the last page of the current Catalog/search results.
List replays ordered by playback count. Only replays with at least one recorded play are included.
Move to the next page of the current Catalog/search results.
Move to the previous page of the current Catalog/search results.
Remove Catalog entries whose replay media can no longer be resolved. It does not delete physical files.
Rate the replay currently playing. Rating is 1 to 5 and is stored per user.
Search the Catalog by text. With no search text, returns the Catalog without a text filter.
Show the current page of the current Catalog/search results.
List replays by rating. 0 is unrated; 1-4 select average rating bands 1.0-4.9; 5 selects a 5.0 average. Without a rating, rated replays are returned ordered by average rating.
Give a Catalog replay a custom title. Custom titles must be unique, ignoring case. The physical video file is not renamed.
Play an item from the Last Played history.
Show recently captured or added replays. This is different from Last Played.
Scan the configured Replay Folder and add replay files that are not already in the Catalog.

sections.title: Create Clip
commands: Request a Kick clip through the KickBot workflow. Kick chat only.
Create a Twitch clip. Twitch chat only. Duration is 5-60 seconds.
Create a timestamped clip from the current YouTube live broadcast. YouTube chat only.
Tell OBS to save the current Replay Buffer. What happens next depends on Replay Source and Playlist settings.

sections.title: Message
commands: Send a message directly to the RTS overlay using the configured Message Behaviour.

sections.title: Playback
commands: Show the most recently played replays.
Move the player to a saved position. Use the saved position tag, not the display name.
Hide the current player without deleting or resetting the replay.
Change playback speed. Accepted range is 0.25 to 4.0.
Show the current player and resume the current video.

sections.title: Playlist
sections.intro: The Playlist is the live playback queue and is separate from the Catalog and playback history.
commands: Add a replay to the Playlist. A replay can be selected by Catalog/search result number, custom title, or platform and user search context.
Remove waiting items while leaving the currently playing item alone.
Remove everything from the Playlist without stopping a replay already playing.
Pause automatic Playlist progression without stopping the current video.
Remove a waiting item by its Playlist position. The currently playing item cannot be removed.
Resume Playlist progression. If nothing is playing and queued items exist, Resume starts the next item.
